messages.content:
Game Master is standing by.

1. New Game — start fresh
2. Load Game — restore a previous save
3. Continue — resume where we left off

New Game.

World: **Earth Invasion** — Day 1. The Silence happened at dawn. 98% of humanity vanished in a soft white light seventeen minutes later. The System appeared shortly after. Alien ships are now in low orbit over every major city.

You are one of the 2% left behind.

---

Your character file already exists from a previous session:

**John Doe** — 28, Leipzig. IT support. Semi-pro footballer until 26, when years of playing through injury compounded into permanent damage. Came to Germany from rural Croatia at 18 with nothing. Built a middle-class life alone. Decisive, reckless, hides depression behind a wide grin.

Use this character, or start fresh?

1. Play as John Doe (keep everything)
2. Create a new character from scratch

Leipzig. Day 1. 06:53.

The knee woke you first. It always does.

You lie still for a moment, running the usual inventory — right knee, dull throb, manageable. Left hip, tighter than yesterday. Ankle fine for now. Your body's version of a morning report.

Then you notice the silence.

Karl-Heine-Straße should have trams by now. Delivery vans. The bakery two floors below opens at six and the smell usually makes it up here. There's nothing. No sound at all except the specific, pressurised quiet of a city holding its breath.

Your phone is dead. Not low battery — the screen simply will not respond.

You get up. Go to the window.

Above the Lindenauer Hafen, something is in the sky that shouldn't be. Not a plane. Not a blimp. Something enormous, sitting at low altitude, motionless — shaped like nothing you have ever seen. It looks grown rather than built: asymmetric, dark, the surface of it textured like the outside of a seed pod or a dried hive. The size of it is wrong. Your brain keeps trying to rescale it to something comprehensible and failing.

It isn't moving. It's just there. Like it has always been there and you simply never looked up before.

Then the window appears.

Floating in your field of vision, semi-transparent, sharp-edged. You blink. It stays.

`SYSTEM — F-RANK AWAKENING COMPLETE`
`Survivor: John Doe`
`Rank: F — Awakened`
`STR 6 · AGI 8 · END 6 · INT 6`
`HP: 100/100 · Mental: 8/100`
`Resonance profile: analysis in progress`
`Active survivors — Leipzig district: 3`

It fades to a thin HUD outline at the edge of your vision. Still there. Not going away.

Three survivors. In all of Leipzig. Including you.

Outside, something that looks like it was grown by something that does not think the way you think is floating over your city, and you are standing at your window in your boxer shorts processing this information.

You have a very strong feeling that the next few decisions matter.

---

1. Check your flat first — take stock of what you have before you do anything else
2. Watch the ship — study it, understand what you can from a distance before moving
3. Leave the building immediately — you want open space and a better vantage point
4. Try the other flats on your floor — see if anyone else is still here

You stay at the window.

IT support habit: when something is broken, you look at it before you touch it. You watch the ship.

It does not move. Not at all — not a drift, not a rotation, not any of the small corrections a mechanical object would make to maintain position. Whatever is keeping it up there requires no visible effort. The surface of it has a very slight texture variation that your eye keeps trying to read as panels or plating but isn't — it's more like grain, like the side of a gourd. Dark amber-brown in the morning light. You estimate the length at roughly two hundred metres, give or take. The underside is wider than the top. No windows you can see. No exhaust. No sound carries to you even with the city this quiet.

Then something detaches from the underside.

Small — human-sized, maybe slightly larger. Dark. It drops and then stabilises, moving horizontally with no visible propulsion, heading toward the city centre. Unhurried. Then a second one separates. Then a third, taking a different angle, toward the Hauptbahnhof area.

They spread out as they go. Systematic. Each moving on its own line. None of them come in your direction.

You watch until they disappear between buildings. The ship doesn't move the whole time.

*Whatever those things are, they are not here for you yet. They went toward the centre.*

You step back from the window.

---

You do a proper sweep of the flat. IT brain, footballer discipline — methodical.

**Kitchen:**
Tap water works. You fill both of your 1.5L sports bottles. Fridge has leftovers, yoghurt, a block of cheese. Cupboards: pasta, two tins of chickpeas, protein powder, half a bag of oats, three protein bars. One decent kitchen knife.

**Living area:**
Laptop — powers on. No internet, but it works. Charger, portable battery bank (60% charge). TV is on but no signal on any channel.

**Sports bag by the door:**
Training kit, spare trainers, shin pads. A roll of sports tape — you use it on the knee and ankle when training gets serious. Foam roller.

**Bathroom cabinet:**
Ibuprofen, knee support brace, plasters, basic first aid.

**Your backpack** — the one you use for work — is empty and ready.

You stand in the middle of your flat. The System HUD is still at the edge of your vision. The city is still silent. Those things are somewhere in the city centre right now, doing something you don't yet understand.

You have maybe thirty minutes before your situation changes in some way. Possibly more. Possibly less.

---

1. Pack and leave now — take what matters, get out, find the other survivors
2. Stay in the flat longer — barricade, observe from the window, gather more information
3. Go knock on doors in the building — the System says 3 survivors in the district, one might be a neighbour
4. Head toward the city centre — see what those things are doing up close

You move fast.

Knee brace first — you strap it on sitting on the bed, wind the sports tape around the ankle twice the way you've done a hundred times before training. You've learned not to skip this step. Your body will let you run on adrenaline for a while, but it will collect the debt later.

Packing is three minutes. You've thought through this kind of scenario more times than you'd admit — it's the IT brain, the same one that documents disaster recovery plans nobody reads until the server is on fire.

Backpack: water bottles, protein bars, chickpeas tins, ibuprofen, first aid kit, sports tape roll (spare), laptop and battery bank. Kitchen knife goes in the side pocket. You put the spare hoodie on — it's cool out and layers matter more than looking normal right now.

You leave the foam roller. Leave the pasta — too much weight for too little return. The cheese and yoghurt won't survive a day without refrigeration anyway.

Phone in your pocket out of habit. Still dead.

---

Karl-Heine-Straße is the wrong kind of empty.

You've seen the street at 3am on a Tuesday. That's a quiet that feels earned — the city resting. This is different. A tram has stopped forty metres to your left, doors open, interior lights still on. Someone's bicycle is lying on its side in the bike lane, wheels still slowly turning from whatever momentum was left when its rider disappeared. A car at the intersection ahead has its engine running, driver's door open.

The ship is directly visible from the street. Larger-seeming now that you're outside — without a window frame to contain it, it just occupies the sky above the Hafen in a way that makes the surrounding buildings look like they're leaning away from it. Still not moving. Still making no sound.

The System HUD pulses once at the edge of your vision. Not a notification — just a flicker, like a signal checking whether you're still there.

You are still there.

The street stretches in both directions. Empty in all of them.

---

1. Head toward the Hafen — get closer to the ship, understand the scale of what you're dealing with
2. Go building to building along Karl-Heine-Straße — look for signs of the other survivors
3. Find higher ground — the church tower on Plagwitzer Straße, get a view of the whole district
4. Head to the nearest supermarket — secure more supplies before anything else

4, find weapons, makeshift explosives, pointy sticks, whatever.

After that 3

The Rewe on Industriestraße is three minutes away. The automatic doors are stuck half-open — power on, sensors not quite working without people moving through them. You slide in through the gap.

The lights are on. The refrigeration units are humming. The store is completely, utterly empty. Someone left a basket on the floor mid-shop — bread rolls, milk, a jar of peanut butter, still sitting there like they stepped away to grab one more thing.

You move efficiently. LitRPG logic applies: early game, before competition, take everything that could matter.

**Food run first** — energy gels from the sports shelf, a bag of mixed nuts, two tins of sardines, a jar of that peanut butter from the abandoned basket. You're not sentimental.

**Then weapons.** And here is where the fantasy diverges from the reality.

This is a German supermarket, not a hardware store. You do what you can.

From the kitchen aisle: a heavy chef's knife, proper steel, better than what you brought. A meat cleaver — not elegant, but the weight is honest.

From the cleaning aisle: a mop. You unscrew the head and test the handle — solid aluminium. Decent reach, decent weight. Not a pointy stick but close enough.

From behind the deli counter: a long bone saw, the kind butchers use. Serrated. Uncomfortable to look at.

From the spirits aisle: two 70cl bottles of cheap vodka, 40%. You know what these are for. You know because you've read enough. From the checkout: a lighter. From the cleaning aisle: a cloth.

*Molotov components. Two of them. Simple, effective at F-rank, and you can make them right now if you need to.*

You also pull the CO2 fire extinguisher from the wall by the staff entrance. Heavy, but it goes in the bag — it can blind, disorient, knock something off balance, buy you three seconds. In a fight at your level, three seconds is everything.

A proper fertiliser bomb or improvised explosive? Not today. That needs chemistry, materials, and time you don't have. The vodka is your ceiling for now.

You're fifteen minutes in the store. Backpack is significantly heavier. You hoist it, feel the weight settle, adjust the straps. The knee doesn't complain yet.

---

The church tower on Plagwitzer Straße is unlocked — the side door swings open when you push it. The staircase is narrow and dark, the kind of dark that smells like old wood and candle wax. Your flashlight from the flat would've been useful here. You use your phone screen on minimum brightness instead. Still dead as a phone. Still glows.

Fifty-one steps. You counted, because that's what you do.

The view from the top stops you.

Leipzig spreads out in every direction, quiet as a photograph. You can see three, four kilometres in the morning air. The ship over the Hafen is enormous from here — you're looking at it almost level with its underside, close enough to make out the texture clearly. The grain of it runs in long irregular lines, like wood but wrong, like something that grew under pressure. It makes no sound. It casts no shadow in the low morning light.

You look toward the city centre.

The catalogers are further than you expected. Much further. They've already crossed the inner ring road — you can just make out two of them moving along Grimmaische Straße, about two kilometres from you. Methodical. One building at a time. They're going to reach the residential neighbourhoods sooner than your mental estimate.

But that's not what makes you go still.

About eight hundred metres northeast, on Josephinenstraße — a window is lit. Third floor, left flat. Not the cold fluorescent of an empty room left on. Warm light. Lamp light. Moving, slightly, like someone is in there.

Someone is home.

---

1. Go to Josephinenstraße — find whoever is in that flat
2. Keep watching from the tower — gather more before you move
3. Head away from the catalogers' direction — put distance between you and them first
4. Go toward the catalogers — get close enough to understand what exactly they're doing
